comments.body: Remediation verified 2026-09-10 09:58, no reboot needed: operator sudo-killed fseventsd (SIP blocks launchctl kickstart; direct signal works, launchd respawns). New fseventsd PID 21316 at 10.9MB RSS (was 28.5GB RSS / 107GB footprint). Swap 67.0/68.6GB -> 18.4/19.4GB and draining; free RAM ~0.1GB -> ~52GB; compressor 65GB -> 39GB. Additional finding for AC1: codex respawns MCP servers ON DEMAND when one dies (observed respawn at 09:57:12 after stale-stack kills), so (a) killing stale stacks is safe for live conversations, and (b) the config enabled=false only takes effect at ChatGPT.app restart — operator to relaunch the app when the current parallel session finishes. AC3 verification window starts now; mem-sentinel snapshots should confirm fseventsd stays <5GB over the week.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

ChatGPT.app codex (single long-lived process, PID 11153 this boot) launches a fresh MCP server stack (uvx serena start-mcp-server --context codex + pyright-langserver + node + headroom mcp wrapper) per conversation epoch and leaves prior stacks running when conversations end. Because codex stays alive, stale stacks keep a live parent (never PPID 1) and evade the mem-sentinel PPID-1 orphan sweeper shipped for centauric-gnomic-hake (7495-36ea-df75-4a3d) — the surviving variant of that defect class. Stale stacks (~1.2GB each; 4 epochs Sep 6/7/9/10 observed) go fully swapped-out and stop draining FSEventStreams while remaining registered clients; under rebar's fs-event volume fseventsd accretes buffers without bound and never returns memory (peak==current): 107GB phys_footprint by day 4 of the Sep 6 boot (27.2GB RSS + 79.8GB swapped, 136.8M live mallocs, 47.8M path strings), swap 67/68.6GB — near-recurrence of incident 2ab6-bae5-8ca4-429c. Claude/Copilot ide-assistant serena instances do not accumulate.

## Approach (remediation executed 2026-09-10, operator-assisted)

1. 4-phase debug confirmed mechanism (hypothesis tests: codex-code-mode-host VSZ = reserved address space, refuted; killing one stale serena freed only its own swap while fseventsd stayed at 107GB peak==current, so reclaim requires daemon restart).
2. Stale Sep 6/7 stacks killed by explicit pid; codex observed respawning MCP servers on demand (09:57:12), so kills are safe for live conversations.
3. Serena disabled for codex in ~/.codex/config.toml (enabled=false, incident annotation); effective at next ChatGPT.app restart since codex respawns from launch-time config.
4. Operator restarted fseventsd via sudo kill (SIP blocks launchctl kickstart; launchd respawns).
5. Monitoring already in place: mem-sentinel logs fseventsdKB every 5 min and reaps PPID-1 orphans; the codex-alive-parent gap is mooted by (3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Serena is disabled for codex: `grep -B1 -A1 'enabled = false' ~/.codex/config.toml` shows the annotated [mcp_servers.serena] block with `enabled = false`.
- [ ] No stale codex serena stacks remain: `ps axo pid,ppid,lstart,args | grep 'serena start-mcp-server' | grep -v grep` shows only current-session instances (each parent uv/codex chain alive and serving a live conversation or agent).
- [ ] fseventsd reclaimed without reboot: `ps -o rss= -p $(pgrep -x fseventsd)` reports < 100MB RSS on a freshly respawned pid.
- [ ] Swap pressure relieved: `sysctl -n vm.swapusage` shows used well below the 67GB incident level (observed 18.4GB post-remediation).
- [ ] Evidence trail durable: findings recorded as comments here and on 2ab6-bae5-8ca4-429c, with raw evidence under .rebar/scratch/memleak-copilot-87759/.

## Testing / Verification

All ACs verified live on the host 2026-09-10 ~09:58 (evidence in comments): fseventsd 107GB -> 10.9MB RSS (new PID 21316), swap used 67GB -> 18.4GB and draining, free RAM ~0.1GB -> ~52GB, compressor 65GB -> 39GB. Ongoing observation is operational via `tail ~/Library/Logs/mem-sentinel.log` (fseventsdKB column), deliberately not a ticket-held wait. No repo code changed; host-config change is ~/.codex/config.toml only, hence no file_impact recorded.
compiled_state.title: Codex spawns one serena/pyright MCP stack per conversation and never reaps old ones — stale FSEvents clients drive fseventsd accretion (2026-09-10 near-exhaustion recurrence)
